newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Gunmen kill five civilians in Somalia.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill five civilians in Somalia.

text.p: Unidentified gunmen firing machineguns ambushed a bus in southern Mogadishu in Somalia on Wednesday, killing five civilians and wounding seven including two women, witnesses said.
They said the bus travelling from Bakara market to Gupta district stopped at a hastily-built roadblock put up by five gunmen who then opened fire, spraying the vehicle with scores of bullets.
A witness said most of the casualties were members of the Murusade sub-clan loyal to Mohamed Kanyare Afrah, interior minister in a government set up by late faction leader Mohamed Farah Aideed.
The motive for the attack was unknown but it raised tension in the area, prompting some gunmen to take to the streets.
Two officials of the Somalfruit Company, a banana exporter, were killed on Tuesday night by unidentified gunmen in Lower Shabelle region 90 km (55 miles) south of Mogadishu, security sources said.
The sources said one of the men was a deputy director of Somalfruit, which exports bananas from areas controlled by Hussein Aideed, who succeeded his father when he died on August 1.
Aideed's government has only been recognised by Libya and Sudan and is opposed by an alliance led by north Mogadishu faction leader Ali Mahdi Mohamed.
Somalia has had no central government since the fall of late dictator Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991.
